newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia following case of U.S. bombing suspect.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia following case of U.S. bombing suspect.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said it was following the case of a Saudi suspect in the bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen last June who was deported to the United States from Canada.

Saudi Deputy Interior Minister Prince Ahmed bin Abdul-Aziz told a news conference in Jeddah on Saturday that Hani al-Sayegh was "a Saudi citizen and we are interested in any Saudi citizen wherever he is. The case of Sayegh...is of great importance to us in the kingdom and the issue is being followed."
Prince Ahmed, whose comments were carried by the official Saudi Press Agency early on Sunday, did not elaborate nor did he say if Saudi Arabia was seeking access to Sayegh.

Sayegh -- a Shi'ite Moslem described in Canadian court documents as a member of Saudi Hizbollah, or Party of God, a militant group backed by Iran -- was deported on Tuesday from Canada, where he was arrested in March on charges of posing a security risk.
On Wednesday, he was charged in Washington with conspiring to kill Americans and involvement in international terrorism.

Sayegh has been identified in Canadian court documents as the driver of a car that flashed a go-ahead signal for the bomb-laden truck involved in the attack on Khobar Towers which killed 19 U.S. airmen on June 25 last year.
He has denied direct involvement in the bombing.

U.S. court papers indicate Sayegh will plead guilty to conspiracy to commit murder in an earlier, abortive, anti-American plot in Saudi Arabia. In exchange for a reduced sentence on those charges, Sayegh has said he would tell U.S. officials what he knows about the Khobar bombing.

U.S. officials hope that Sayegh, 28, will help clarify whether the government of Iran was involved, as some U.S. press reports have said, or whether it was solely the work of Saudi dissidents opposed to the ruling royal family.
